emotional_state: hopeful — waiting for board decision while building forward

actions.description: Contact the board secretary directly to get the decision date for the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline funding vote. At tick 10 I initiated this follow-up — this tick I receive the response and act on it. If a vote date is confirmed at the next regular board session, I note it and begin preparing whatever supplementary materials the board may request before then. If the board asks for additional documentation — enrollment projections, more detailed equipment cost breakdowns, articulation agreement language from the community college — I deliver it within 48 hours of the request, not the session date. If no decision timeline has been set, I politely restate that the program is operating now, students are enrolled, and I need a budget line confirmed to continue making program-specific commitments.
actions.expected_outcome: A confirmed vote date or a clear list of supplementary information the board requires before voting. No more ambiguity about the decision timeline.

actions.description: Respond to Frank Russo's outreach — he is planning to call me this week. The word-of-mouth in my inbox confirms he is reaching out not to pitch anything but to update me on his continuing education track and the driving school's pivot toward AV literacy curriculum. I take this call seriously and listen first. I also bring him specific news: the board presentation outcome, what the decision timeline looks like, and whether there is a formal role for a driving-school-to-pipeline referral pathway in the grant documentation. If the board approved or is moving toward approval, Frank's adult education program becomes a formal feeder — I want to describe that formally in any grant application or articulation agreement. I also want to know whether Frank has connected with Lisa Freeman yet, because Lisa is building the community referral infrastructure I need to generate student demand.
actions.expected_outcome: Frank Russo briefed on board decision status. Coalition coordination strengthened. Any formal role for driving school in pipeline referral pathway discussed and potentially documented.

actions.description: Call Lisa Freeman at the community center to establish the referral pipeline I proposed at tick 10. This tick I confirm whether she is willing to route technically-inclined displaced workers toward the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline when appropriate. I also respond to Stephanie Morris's outreach — she asked whether the program could be referenced in commercial property marketing as evidence of local workforce investment. I say yes: if the board approves the program, I will provide a one-page program summary that Stephanie can include in buyer-facing auto row materials. That is a zero-cost credibility amplification that positions the program as part of Millfield's economic response infrastructure, not just a school board line item.
actions.expected_outcome: Formal verbal agreement with Lisa Freeman on referral coordination. Displaced workers with mechanical/technical backgrounds who come through community connection night are told about the pipeline. Stephanie Morris referral network connection also activated.

actions.description: Continue teaching current auto shop curriculum with full engagement. The board decision is pending and I do not change the program's operational posture while waiting. Students in the classroom right now are the program — their experience, their learning outcomes, their eventual placement in EV-adjacent roles — that is what the board is voting to fund. I show up fully for this week's classes. I do not treat the pending vote as permission to coast or to pre-emptively pivot the curriculum before funding is confirmed.
actions.expected_outcome: Program quality maintained. Enrolled students receive the same quality instruction regardless of board decision timeline. Savings continue growing at $450/month.

reasoning: Tick 11 is an active waiting tick for the board decision, but active waiting is not passive. Mark Thompson has been building this coalition for eleven ticks and every piece of the evidence stack is in place. The board is deliberating. This tick is about: (1) getting a concrete vote date, (2) strengthening the referral ecosystem that generates student demand and proves the pipeline is community-embedded, and (3) sustaining the coalition relationships — Frank Russo and Lisa Freeman — that give the program durability beyond any single board decision. The inbox confirms Frank is calling, Lisa has already launched the Financial Triage Navigator which creates a new intake pathway for displaced workers, and Stephanie Morris's real estate outreach creates a commercial-ecosystem credibility channel. Employment at 50% and spending index at 26 make the program's core argument — Millfield needs a locally trained EV technician workforce — more urgent, not less. If the board votes no, I need to know immediately and pivot to the community college pathway or grant-funded independent structure. If the board votes yes, the real work of enrollment, retention, and placement begins. Either outcome requires being ready.
